newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran produces daily newspaper for the blind.
newsitem.headline: Iran produces daily newspaper for the blind.

text.p: Blind people in Iran now have a daily Persian-language newspaper in Braille.
The backers of the daily Iran Sepid -- which means white -- say it is the first of its kind in the Middle East.
Sepid has built a subscriber base of 5,000 readers since its launch on November 18, a source close to the paper said.
"The purpose is to meet the needs of the blind, reaching them in terms of the information they need," he said.
Editorial staff offer their skills free of charge.
The paper's backer, the Persian-language morning daily Iran, is aiming to publish an English-language version of the Braille paper as well as a yearbook.

Iran editor Hussein Ziaei was reported this month as saying Iran Sepid was the most important step for the publishing group, which also plans to launch English and Arabic-language versions of Iran and produce dailies covering sport and youth issues.
